title: The World Wars
tagline: Two wars, the revolutions of 1917, the interwar dictatorships, occupation, and the genocide of the Jews
summary: This course runs from 1914 to the German surrender in May 1945. It includes the home fronts and the soldiers of empire, the two calendars of 1917, the fragile settlements of 1919, the dictatorships of the 1930s, occupation, and the murder of about six million Jews. It does not sort nations into the guilty and the innocent.
overview: The First World War is dated by Verdun, the Somme, the American entry, Brest-Litovsk and the armistice, without invented casualty totals. The revolutions of 1917 are dated in both calendars. Versailles is one treaty among the Paris settlements, signed in the same hall where the German Empire had been proclaimed.

The interwar chapter includes Italy, the USSR, the German slump, Hitler’s appointment, and the Spanish Civil War. It does not reduce the years 1918–1939 to a corridor leading to one man. The war chapter follows Poland, France, the Soviet Union, occupation, and the dates of surrender, including the difference between 8 May and 9 May.

The genocide chapter uses the estimate of about six million Jews, the date of Wannsee as a coordination meeting rather than a beginning, and the coining of the word genocide. It names other victim groups without inventing totals. It does not describe killing procedures.
outcomes: Place Verdun, the Somme, Brest-Litovsk and the armistice without inventing a death total.
Give both dates of the October Revolution and say why both are used.
Distinguish the Treaty of Versailles from the other Paris treaties, and name two interwar dictatorships besides Germany.
Order the European war from 1 September 1939 to the surrenders of May 1945, including 22 June 1941.
Explain why Wannsee is not the start of the Holocaust, and use the figure of about six million Jews as an estimate.

history.title: Two calendars
history.detail: The October Revolution is 25 October 1917 on the Julian calendar and 7 November 1917 on the Gregorian. Russia moves its civil calendar the next year.

history.title: Versailles
history.detail: The treaty is signed on 28 June 1919 in the Hall of Mirrors. It is one of the Paris settlements, not the whole of the peace.

history.title: Appointment
history.detail: Hitler is appointed chancellor on 30 January 1933. The Enabling Act follows on 23 March, after the Reichstag fire of 27 February.

history.title: Wannsee
history.detail: On 20 January 1942 officials meet at Wannsee to coordinate deportation and murder. Mass killing has already begun. The figure of about six million Jewish dead is an estimate used by historians and by memorial institutions.
